summary.text: Itô calculus, named after Kiyosi Itô, extends the methods of calculus to stochastic processes such as Brownian motion.
Ordinary calculus does not work on Brownian paths, because they are not differentiable at any point and have infinite variation over every time interval.
It has important applications in mathematical finance, in stochastic differential equations, and more recently even in machine learning.

facts.label: Key condition
facts.value: The integrand must be adapted to information available so far

facts.label: Where sums sample
facts.value: Typically the left end of each small interval

facts.label: Main results
facts.value: Integration by parts and Itô's lemma

facts.label: Rival version
facts.value: The Stratonovich integral follows the ordinary chain rule

items.prompt: A trader's rule says what to hold at time t, and it may use only information available up to time t. Why does the theory insist on this?

options.label: It makes every trade profitable
It stops the stock price from changing
It makes trades happen faster
It rules out unlimited gains from knowing the next move

items.explain: Requiring the integrand to be adapted prevents unlimited gains through clairvoyance, such as buying just before each uptick and selling before each downtick.

items.prompt: A student tries to apply the usual derivative-based tools of calculus to the path of a Brownian particle. Why does this fail?

options.label: The path has no starting point
The path is too smooth to have a slope
The path is not differentiable at any point
The path never moves at all

items.explain: Brownian paths fail the requirements for standard calculus: they are not differentiable at any point and have infinite variation over every time interval.

items.prompt: In school calculus, a change of variables adds just one slope term. For Brownian motion an extra second-derivative term appears. Where does it come from?

options.label: Brownian motion has non-zero quadratic variation
Brownian motion is smoother than ordinary functions
Brownian motion always moves in a straight line
Brownian motion forgets the information it has seen

items.explain: Itô's lemma differs from the standard result because of the extra term involving the second derivative, which comes from Brownian motion having non-zero quadratic variation.

items.prompt: A student wants a stochastic integral that obeys the ordinary chain rule and needs no special lemma. Which one should they pick?

options.label: The Itô integral
The Stratonovich integral
A Riemann sum with a single interval
A sum using only the left ends

items.explain: The Stratonovich integral follows the chain rule and does not require Itô's lemma, while the Itô integral does not follow it.

items.prompt: In the trading reading of an Itô integral, which part stands for how much stock we hold at each moment?

options.label: The integrand
The integrator
The total money we end up with
The size of the time interval

items.explain: The integrand is how much stock we hold, the integrator represents the movement of the prices, and the integral is the total money including the stock's worth.

items.prompt: You compute the Itô integral from 0 to a fixed time t of a random process. What kind of thing do you get?

options.label: A single fixed number every time
A random variable, defined as a limit of random variables
A straight line through the origin
A smooth curve with a slope at every point

items.explain: The integral up to a particular time is a random variable, defined as a limit of a sequence of random variables, and the result of the integration is another stochastic process.
